summary.title: How to Scope a New Feature For Your Product
summary.one_liner: You learn a phased feature-ticket template (Planning, Alpha, Beta, GA, Post-GA) that ties each release stage to success metrics and exit criteria, illustrated with a Chuckwagon app-review example.
takeaways: Break a new feature into Planning, Alpha, Beta, GA and Post-GA phases, each with defined owners and tasks.
Define customer and business success metrics before work starts, and write a draft press release as an alignment check.
Set explicit exit criteria for each phase (e.g., metric lift and sample sizes) to decide whether to advance.
Invest in later phases only in proportion to the quantitative and qualitative evidence gathered earlier.
Run a retrospective after launch to check whether goals were met and record lessons learned.
summary.summary: The article presents a feature ticket template borrowed from Google's release style, split into Planning, Alpha, Beta, General Availability and Post-GA phases, with tasks tagged by owning function (Product, Design, Engineering, Marketing, Sales, Customer Success). It walks through a worked example of a fictional app, Chuckwagon, aiming for 5-star average app store reviews, showing concrete Alpha and Beta exit criteria such as rating averages, review counts and Download Rate lift. It closes by tying the approach to the "Invest Proportionate to Confidence" idea. The page is an excerpt from a longer paid Google Doc that includes more commentary and an example user story.
